title: [tenmin-history] countGappedPlannedFetches: characterization test for counting gapped planned fetches
body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

add a characterization test for countGappedPlannedFetches in src/tenmin-history.ts: gapped planned fetches
- countGappedPlannedFetches([{ securityId: "S", symbol: "A", fetchFrom: "f", fetchTo: "t" }], [{ securityId: "S", symbol: "A", reason: "r", at: "x", fetchFrom: "f", fetchTo: "t" }]) is 1
- countGappedPlannedFetches([{ securityId: "S", symbol: "A", fetchFrom: "f", fetchTo: "t" }], [{ securityId: "S", symbol: "B", reason: "r", at: "x", fetchFrom: "f", fetchTo: "t" }]) is 0
- countGappedPlannedFetches([{ securityId: "S", symbol: "A", fetchFrom: "f", fetchTo: "t" }], [{ securityId: "S", symbol: "A", reason: "r", at: "x" }]) is 0

(Builder pre-file, TEST_CASE_EXISTING, public-test-case-existing-v2): Peace's task (source: peace). The gapped-fetch count behind the ten-minute range remaining estimate is never called directly by a test; this pins that a gap counts only when it matches a planned fetch and carries its fetch window. Production safety: test-only: one new src/*.test.ts file only: no source edits, no fix commit. Job B grades it fix-free: the test passes on the current code and fails with the function body stubbed. The running scanner chain is unchanged. A box dry-run on PeaceSTOCKS 5c41528 (Workspace main efd3f76, Node 22) built exactly one candidate (public-test-case-existing-v2); a local Job B run graded it COUNTS (the new test passes on the current code and fails with countGappedPlannedFetches stubbed); suite 564/564 with all eight new tests of this batch, all 4 typechecks ok. Disjoint file: each task in this batch creates its own new test file. Expected COUNTS.)
